Make a factor, or count values, in parallel

Source: R/par-factor.R
par_factor.Rd

Drop-in replacements for base functions, faster for large inputs:

  • par_factor() for factor().

  • par_table() for table().

They take base's arguments and give identical results. The only differences: both take nthreads, and par_factor() ignores nmax.

Usage

par_factor(
  x = character(),
  levels,
  labels = levels,
  exclude = NA,
  ordered = is.ordered(x),
  nmax = NA,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

par_table(
  ...,
  exclude = if (useNA == "no") c(NA, NaN),
  useNA = c("no", "ifany", "always"),
  dnn = list_names(...),
  deparse.level = 1,
  nthreads = getOption("parvenu.threads", 0L)
)

Arguments

x

A vector, as in base::factor().

levels

an optional vector of the unique values (as character strings) that x might have taken. The default is the unique set of values taken by as.character(x), sorted into increasing order of x. Note that this set can be specified as smaller than sort(unique(x)).

labels

either an optional character vector of labels for the levels (in the same order as levels after removing those in exclude), or a character string of length 1. Duplicated values in labels can be used to map different values of x to the same factor level.

exclude

a vector of values to be excluded when forming the set of levels. This may be factor with the same level set as x or should be a character.

ordered

logical flag to determine if the levels should be regarded as ordered (in the order given).

nmax

Ignored. It is a hint for base's hash table, kept so that the arguments are in base's order.

nthreads

A whole number: the max number of threads to use. 0 means the RAYON_NUM_THREADS environment variable, or else all cores. The default is the parvenu.threads option, or 0 if that isn't set. Inputs too small to keep that many threads busy get fewer, and more threads than cores count as all cores.

...

Vectors or factors of the same length, or a single list of them, such as a data frame, as in base::table().

useNA

whether to include NA values in the table. See ‘Details’. Can be abbreviated.

dnn

the names to be given to the dimensions in the result (the dimnames names).

deparse.level

controls how the default dnn is constructed. See ‘Details’.

Value

As base: a factor from par_factor(), a table from par_table().

Details

Both spend most of their time finding the distinct values and the position of each element among them. Here, par_unique() and par_match() do that on several threads, and par_table() counts the cells on several threads too. Sorting the levels stays with base R.

factor() of 1e7 strings in 1e5 levels takes about 0.8s in base R and 0.5s here, most of it sorting the levels. For 1e7 integers in 1e6 levels, 0.85s becomes 0.3s, most of it making the levels' strings. table() of 1e7 integers in 1e4 levels takes about 0.25s in base and 20ms here; of a factor with 100 levels, 80ms and 5ms.

A double vector is tabulated by its printed values, as in base. That takes seconds for 1e7 of them either way.

Examples

par_factor(c("b", "a", "b"))
#> [1] b a b
#> Levels: a b
par_factor(c(3, 1, 3), labels = c("low", "high"))
#> [1] high low  high
#> Levels: low high
par_table(c("b", "a", "b", NA), useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#>    a    b <NA> 
#>    1    2    1 
par_table(c(1, 2, 1), c("x", "x", "y"))
#>    
#>     x y
#>   1 1 1
#>   2 1 0
